plain.text: Five days later the high priest Ananias came to Caesarea with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who brought charges against Paul before Felix. After flattering the governor, Tertullus said Paul was a troublemaker who stirred up riots among the Jews all over the world, a ringleader of the Nazarene sect, and had tried to desecrate the temple. The others agreed.

Paul answered. He said he had gone up to Jerusalem to worship only twelve days earlier and had not stirred up any crowd. They could not prove their charges. "I admit that I worship the God of our ancestors as a follower of the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything in the Law and the Prophets, and I have the same hope in God as these men, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked." He always tried to keep his conscience clear before God and people. He had come bringing gifts for the poor. The only thing he had shouted was, "It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial."

Felix, who knew about the Way, adjourned the case. He kept Paul under guard but gave him some freedom and let his friends care for him. Later Felix and his wife Drusilla sent for Paul and listened as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus. When Paul talked about righteousness, self-control and the judgement to come, Felix was afraid and said, "That's enough for now! I'll send for you when it's convenient." He hoped Paul would offer him a bribe, so he talked with him often. After two years, Festus replaced Felix, but Felix left Paul in prison to please the Jewish leaders.

summary.bigIdea: Paul defends himself honestly before Governor Felix, who hears the message but puts off responding.
points: Paul is falsely accused of causing riots and desecrating the temple.
He calmly explains his faith and his hope in the resurrection.
Felix becomes afraid when Paul speaks of righteousness and judgement, and says "when it's convenient".
summary.reflection: Felix kept putting off a decision. Is there something God has been asking of you that you've been putting off?
